encyclopedia.summary: CD Projekt RED's first Witcher game, released in 2007 and based on Andrzej Sapkowski's novels. Geralt, a monster hunter without his memory, is forced to choose between kingdom politics and the trade of killing monsters. Choices that do not show their result immediately and come back later became the series' signature.
highlights: Established delayed consequences as the series' basic structure.
Ties monster contracts and political intrigue into the same job format.
Widely read as the first Western game adaptation of a Polish novel.

related.note: Sequel — choices grow to the scale of nations

encyclopedia.summary: BioWare's 2009 role-playing game about betrayal in the kingdom of Ferelden and the Blight. You begin as a human noble, an elf, a dwarf or a mage, and the opening hours change completely with that origin. Relationships with companions and political choices shape the ending, and it set the standard for Western RPGs of the 2000s.
highlights: Six origin stories give six different openings and social vantage points.
Companion approval and political choices decide who stands where at the end.
Real-time-with-pause combat puts the weight on party composition and tactics.

encyclopedia.summary: An open-world action game made by Ubisoft Montreal in 2014. Aiden Pearce, who can hack a city's surveillance infrastructure, hunts the organisation behind his family's death. It leans on cameras, traffic lights and signals to set up a fight rather than on shooting first.
highlights: Combat is designed around changing what the enemy can see and where they can move.
It takes surveillance and privacy as its subject, then settles into a revenge story.
It was an early attempt to treat a whole city as hackable data.
